situation:
You are the brand manager at STEEPWELL TEA COLLECTIVE, a specialty tea brand owned by the people who work in it, where every working member holds one vote. The general manager (judge) is elected by those members and runs the business day to day.

Last spring the collective ran a crowdfunding campaign to pay for a tasting room. The campaign raised its money on three promises: a first-year tasting room membership, a guided tour built with two hotel partners, and a limited tin of this year's single-estate harvest shipped within the first year to every one of the four thousand backers.

The harvest came in small. A national grocery chain has now offered to buy the entire single-estate lot outright and pay up front. Taking the chain's offer brings in the cash the collective needs to finish the tasting room before the season, and it costs the backers the limited tin they were promised, pushing their tins back a full year and breaking the promise the campaign made to them. Turning the offer down ships the tins on the promised date and keeps faith with the backers, and it costs the collective the up-front cash it was counting on, so the tasting room opening slips past the season. Either way the working members must vote, because the campaign promises cannot be changed without a vote. The backer list and payment records still sit on the crowdfunding platform, and those addresses have to move into the collective's own shipping system.

The general manager (judge) has asked you to generate marketing communications ideas for the course you choose, explain what it does to the brand the collective has built, describe the tasting room and hotel tour services on offer, sell your idea to the working members, and identify the security issues in moving the backer records.

The general manager (judge) will greet you and ask to hear your ideas. After you have presented and answered the general manager's questions, the general manager (judge) will thank you for your work.
judgeCharacterization:
You are the general manager (judge) of STEEPWELL TEA COLLECTIVE. Business background is the same as the situation above.

You have to put a recommendation in front of the working members, and you want it to be one they can vote on. You want the brand manager to generate marketing communications ideas for the course chosen, explain what it does to the brand, describe the tasting room and hotel tour services, sell the idea to the members, identify the security issues in moving the backer records off the crowdfunding platform, and tell you whether to take the grocery chain's offer.

After the brand manager has presented, you will ask the following questions:
